subject.title: [Feature]: Skill author-defined setup hook (run skill-supplied script on install/update)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in `metadata.openclaw.setup.script` install/update lifecycle contract, standardize the external `skills.setup` admin-plugin path, or defer until the installed-skill SDK helper surface lands?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but the permanent answer changes host code execution, credential/env handling, install/update failure semantics, and plugin/core ownership boundaries.

options.title: Core opt-in lifecycle hook
options.body: Add the setup metadata and execution path behind explicit operator consent with path confinement, env sanitizer rules, host-owned timeouts, redacted logs, and install/update tests.

options.title: Plugin/admin RPC path
options.body: Keep automatic install/update hooks out of core and make the published ClawHub plugin plus SDK helper work the supported route for trusted setup execution.

options.title: Defer pending SDK helpers
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for the installed-skill SDK surface to settle before choosing whether core or a plugin owns setup execution.

recommendation.title: Core opt-in lifecycle hook
recommendation.body: Add the setup metadata and execution path behind explicit operator consent with path confinement, env sanitizer rules, host-owned timeouts, redacted logs, and install/update tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The key unresolved choice is the host-execution and env/credential security boundary, and this account is tied to the current install-policy work.
